newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt raises price of high-quality Giza 45 cotton.
newsitem.headline: Egypt raises price of high-quality Giza 45 cotton.

text.p: Egypt has increased this year's export price of the high-quality Giza 45 cotton variety to 1,000 pounds ($295) per qantar from 700 pounds per qantar last year, officials and exporters said on Thursday.
One Egyptian qantar is equivalent to 50 kg.

Minister of Supply Ahmed Gueily was quoted in Thursday's official press as saying that Japanese importers have agreed to buy almost all the Giza 45 harvest and exporters said the government had increased the price to encourage its production.
"There is a great need for Giza 45 abroad and it is a very high quality strain but it's also expensive to plant," a major exporter told Reuters.
"The government wants the farmers to plant as much as possible so it's encouraging them with this price," he said.
The exporters said that one acre of Giza 45 cotton costs 2,700 pounds and yields about 150 kg of cotton. Other varieties yield twice and three times as much per acre and cost slightly less to plant.
Last season, Egypt produced 360,000 tonnes of cotton. It said it would export 125,000 to 150,000 tonnes but only 62,093 tonnes have been sold 19 weeks into the marketing season.
This year Egypt said it would increase by 100,000 acres to one million acres the area planted with cotton. It forecast this area would yield 400,000 tonnes of cotton.
Egyptian Agriculture Minister Youssef Wali has also said the government would continue to pay farmers 500 pounds a qantar for their cotton this year.
This minimum price, which is slightly higher than average world prices, helped push production last year but kept private-sector traders out of the cotton market.
